title: The 25 Best Strikers in World Soccer—Ranked
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By SI FC StaffOct 9, 2025Harry Kane’s greatness was confirmed with the Ballon d’Or. / Grzegorz Wajda/SOPA Images/LightRocket/Getty ImagesYou can have the most technically gifted full back, the toughest box-to-box midfielder, and the smoothest playmaker—but none of it truly matters without a striker who knows how to find the back of the net.

The game has evolved, and so have the roles of strikers. They’re no longer just goal scorers but multi-dimensional players contributing in all areas. Still, scoring goals remains the ultimate currency.
While the best strikers aren’t judged solely on their tally, many still produce breathtaking numbers season after season.
Here’s Sports Illustrated’s definitive ranking of the top 25 strikers in the world right now.

Patrik Schick isn’t the most glamorous center forward. / Joris Verwijst/Soccrates/Getty ImagesPatrik Schick is the definition of “great touch for a big lad.” He may look gangly and slightly awkward, but his technique tells a very different story.After a few quieter seasons, the Czech international rediscovered his best form in 2024–25, stepping up brilliantly while Victor Boniface was sidelined with injury.Schick grabbed the opportunity with both hands, scoring 27 goals in all competitions and establishing himself as Bayer Leverkusen’s first-choice striker. So impressive was his resurgence that Boniface departed the following summer, while Schick added another 22 goals the next season.

Ollie Watkins is now playing in the Middle East. / Abdullah Ahmed/Getty ImagesIt’s no coincidence that Aston Villa’s remarkable rise coincided with Ollie Watkins’ arrival in 2020.Signed from then-Championship side Brentford, Watkins made the step up look effortless, quickly becoming a reliable source of goals—including a remarkable 27-goal haul in 2023–24.Before he arrived, Villa had narrowly avoided relegation, finishing 17th. Since then, their league finishes have been 11th, 14th, 7th, 4th, 6th and 4th, transforming them from relegation candidates into genuine Champions League contenders and even quarterfinalists in 2024–25.Watkins obviously wasn’t solely responsible, but his contribution was enormous. He’s now taken his talents to Saudi Pro League outfit Al Hilal.

Nicolas Jackson is flying at Aston Villa. / Carl Recine/Getty ImagesNicolas Jackson was deemed by many as a failure at Chelsea, but the numbers tell a different story. Sure, he wasn’t the most ruthless in west London, but he still put up 30 goals across his two campaigns with the club—all the more impressive considering there were frequent managerial changes in the dugout. The striker’s speed, physicality and engine have always made him an absolute handful for Premier League defenses, and those in the Bundesliga discovered similar during his time on loan at Bayern Munich. He scored eight times despite being solely used as Harry Kane’s understudy. Now back in England with Aston Villa, the Senegal international has swiftly established himself as Unai Emery’s first-choice No. 9, and he’s rewarding his former Villarreal coach with some stellar individual showings.

Cristiano Ronaldo continues to defy the aging process. / Fayez NURELDINE/AFP/Getty ImagesYes, he might be in his forties, and yes, he’s now plying his trade in the Saudi Pro League—but Cristiano Ronaldo’s eye for goal and winning mentality remain as sharp as ever.Whether with Al Nassr or Portugal—before his recent international retirement—the prolific veteran will find the back of the net when delivered the proper service. What he lacks in mobility, he makes up for with supreme efficiency in the opposition penalty area. No matter the stage, when Ronaldo, soccer’s first billionaire, plays, he scores. He’s an anomaly. A goalscoring machine. One of the greatest of all time.

Viktor Gyökeres is a pure goalscorer. / Mike Egerton/PA Images/Getty ImagesNinety-seven goals. That’s how many Viktor Gyökeres scored in just two seasons with Sporting CP, helping the club win back-to-back league titles. Yes, 97.It’s a ridiculous number—unmatched by any other player in world soccer over the same period and one of the most prolific scoring stretches in recent history.His move to Arsenal was inevitably less productive by comparison, but 21 goals in all competitions and 14 in the Premier League is hardly a failure. More importantly, his goals came when they mattered, with Gyökeres playing a decisive role in helping the Gunners finally end their 22-year wait for a Premier League title.He couldn’t keep scoring at Sporting’s absurd rate, but he still delivered exactly what Arsenal needed: goals when it mattered most.

Igor Thiago is ever so clinical. / Kevin Hodgson/MI News/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesWhen Ivan Toney left Brentford for the Saudi Pro League, the Bees moved quickly to find his replacement, spending heavily on Igor Thiago despite the Brazilian having little experience at the highest level. The transfer was agreed in February 2024, but a serious preseason knee injury delayed his Brentford debut until May 2025.The wait proved worthwhile. Thiago wasted little time settling into the role of Brentford’s new attacking focal point, showing the same ruthless finishing that had made him such an intriguing prospect.He ended his first Premier League campaign with an outstanding 22 goals, finishing second in the scoring charts behind only Erling Haaland.

Injuries are Benjamin Šeško’s only barrier to success. / Joe Prior/Visionhaus/Getty ImagesBenjamin Šeško has long been the darling of fans and transfer obsessives, who have touted the Slovenian as a future superstar. For a while, though, the hype outpaced the production.That changed in 2024–25, when Šeško finally delivered on his enormous potential, scoring 21 goals in all competitions for RB Leipzig. His first season at Manchester United in 2025–26 followed a similar trajectory: a slow start gave way to a blistering finish, with the striker scoring nine goals in his final 14 Premier League appearances to help the Red Devils secure third place.With his aerial dominance, genuine two-footed finishing and razor-sharp movement inside the box, Šeško increasingly looks like the real deal.The hype was enormous. Now the goals are starting to match it.

Kai Havertz always divides opinion. / David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesKai Havertz has rarely evaded scrutiny during his time in England. Many argue he’s not a natural No. 9—which is somewhat accurate—and he’s unlikely to ever post 30+ goals in a single campaign. But the German, who scored the winning goal in the 2021 Champions League final with Chelsea, offers so much more than just penalty box instincts. Since joining Arsenal, he’s been essential to the club’s resurgence with his clever movement around center backs and beautiful link-up play. A devastating false nine, he’s exceptional at creating space for himself and, more crucially, his attacking teammates. Goals are not in short supply, either. The first two seasons with the Gunners brought a total of 29, while he proved important down the stretch of a Premier League title-winning campaign in 2025–26, scoring seven times in all competitions after returning from a lengthy injury midway through the term—including another Champions League final goal.

Donyell Malen is loving life in Italy’s capital. / Mark Cosgrove/News Images/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesDonyell Malen was a dangerous player at Borussia Dortmund and Aston Villa, but his pace was often used from out wide, limiting the best parts of his game.Since moving to AS Roma, however, Malen has flourished through the middle. His explosive speed, intelligent movement, ability to run in behind and clinical finishing have made him a nightmare for defenders.He scored 14 goals in 18 Serie A appearances during his first half-season in Italy, and the goals haven’t slowed down in 2026–27. Malen finally looks like he’s playing in the position that brings out the very best in him—and Rome has quickly fallen in love.

An underappreciated center forward. / Ricardo Larreina/Europa Press/Getty ImagesMikel Oyarzabal has spent long stretches operating out wide for Real Sociedad and Spain, but it’s through the middle where he’s enjoyed the best form of his career. The Euro 2024 final-winning goalscorer is incredibly clinical, yet also capable of facilitating others around him. He’s something of an enigma. Despite having no one individual attribute that stands out, Oyarzabal has long been among the leading forwards in La Liga, and he was instrumental to Spain winning the 2026 World Cup, too. Boasting incredible technique, supreme intelligence and a keen eye for goal, the versatile striker continues to go underappreciated—perhaps due to his Basque loyalty, which has seen him spend his entire career at Real Sociedad rather than one of Europe’s elite.

Serhou Guirassy was a late bloomer. / Hendrik Deckers/Borussia Dortmund/Getty ImagesSerhou Guirassy’s rise has been nothing short of remarkable.In just a few years, the Guinean has gone from a struggling Ligue 2 striker to a world-class goalscorer who finds the net with remarkable consistency.His breakthrough came on loan at Stuttgart in 2022–23, where he scored 14 goals in 28 games. The move was made permanent, and he exploded the following season with 30 goals in 30 appearances, earning a move to Borussia Dortmund.He was even better in his debut campaign at Signal Iduna Park, scoring 38 goals, including 13 in the Champions League, to finish as the competition’s top scorer and cement his status among the elite. Another 22 goals followed the next season, proving the breakout was no fluke.

Robert Lewandowski signed a two-year contract in Chicago. / Leonardo Fernandez/Getty ImagesRobert Lewandowski may now be plying his trade in Major League Soccer with Chicago Fire, but honestly, he probably didn’t need to leave Europe just yet.Now well into his veteran years, the Polish striker is still getting the job done. In 2025–26, he scored 19 goals in all competitions as Barcelona won La Liga for the second straight season, despite no longer being an automatic starter.Across four seasons at Barça, Lewandowski scored 120 goals in 193 appearances, won three La Liga titles and earned three Team of the Season selections. Even as his role diminished, his finishing remained a cut above.At his age, there may be fewer minutes in the legs—but there are still plenty of goals in the boots.

The Thurams know how to play soccer. / Pim Waslander/Soccrates/Getty ImagesWell, what a free transfer Marcus Thuram has turned out to be for Inter Milan.The Frenchman arrived in the fashion capital of the world off the back of some eye-catching seasons with Borussia Mönchengladbach and settled into Italian soccer without missing a beat.Stepping into the void left by Romelu Lukaku, Thuram quickly formed a formidable partnership with Lautaro Martínez and became a key part of Inter’s 2023–24 and 2025–26 Scudetto-winning sides. He has scored more than 50 goals across all competitions for the Nerazzurri, while his link-up play, hold-up ability and versatility to drift wide have made him a nightmare for defenders.For a player who arrived for nothing, Thuram has delivered an awful lot of something. Brilliant business by Inter.

Liverpool have missed Hugo Ekitiké during his time out with injury. / Jean Catuffe/Getty ImagesA move to Eintracht Frankfurt proved transformative for Hugo Ekitiké, who had struggled to find his footing at PSG after an early big-money switch from Reims in 2022.The Frenchman rediscovered the flair and confidence that once marked him as a rising star. With Omar Marmoush departing for Manchester City, Ekitiké stepped up superbly—thriving in the Bundesliga's open spaces and showcasing his elegant movement, sharp finishing, and deceptive strength.That breakout 2024–25 campaign earned him a move to Liverpool, where he immediately looked at home before an injury interrupted a hugely encouraging debut season.Once fully fit, there’s little reason to think Ekitiké won’t pick up exactly where he left off.

Matheus Cunha is such a clever soccer player. / Marc Atkins/Getty ImagesMatheus Cunha is an absolute joy to watch.The Brazilian can do just about everything: drift inside to pick up the ball and split defenses with a pass, glide through challenges, burst in behind to finish calmly, or unleash a curling effort from distance. And he does it all with a swagger that is unmistakably Cunha.His brilliance for Wolves in 2024–25 was arguably the biggest reason they survived relegation, with the Brazilian carrying their attack almost single-handedly at times. A move to Manchester United followed, where the goals and flair continued to flow.And Wolves? Without their star man, they unsurprisingly went down.
